name: ヴェジタブルカフェ&シーフードバー サイエン (Vegetable Cafe & Seafood Bar Saien)

claims.text: Fried items (soft-shell crab burger, fried shrimp, miso cutlet) are on the menu and likely share kitchen fryers with other dishes. No dedicated GF fryer information is publicly available.

Soy-based dressings are offered on salads, and soy sauce is a standard ingredient in Japanese cuisine — standard Japanese soy sauce (醤油) contains wheat. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternatives are mentioned.
The kitchen prepares raw oysters, wagyu beef, seafood, and fried items alongside vegetable dishes. No separation between vegan and omnivore prep is indicated.

No allergy handling protocol is mentioned on any official or third-party platform. Phone reservations are accepted at 052-212-8553, which would be the best avenue to inquire about specific dietary needs before visiting.
The restaurant's concept emphasizes self-cultivated organic vegetables and daily fresh market seafood, suggesting ingredient quality awareness even if formal allergy protocols are not advertised.

name: 和風ラザニア専門店 Y (Wafu Razania Senmonten Wai (Japanese-Style L)

claims.text: Wheat pasta is the foundational ingredient of every dish; cross-contamination throughout the kitchen is near-certain. No separate preparation areas for allergen-free cooking are documented.

Soy sauce (which contains wheat) is used directly in the lasagna sauce blend alongside Hatchomiso. Wheat is present in both the pasta layers and the sauce itself — there is no wheat-free version of any menu item.
Dairy (béchamel/white sauce, cheese) and meat proteins are core to the menu; no vegan preparation track exists. Cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.

name: やきとり 風月 名古屋本店 (Yakitori Fugetsu Nagoya Honten)

claims.text: No information on cross-contamination protocols is publicly available. The kitchen handles wheat-containing tare sauce, soy sauce-based dressings, and wheat noodle finishing dishes in the same space as the grill — cross-contamination risk for celiacs must be assumed until directly confirmed otherwise.

Standard tare (焼き鳥のたれ) used on skewers almost certainly contains soy sauce brewed with wheat. Sesame-ponzu dishes and other à la carte items also likely use wheat-containing soy sauce. No tamari or gluten-free soy sauce option is mentioned anywhere across sources.

The entire menu is built around chicken and meat; animal products are present in every course element including broths, tare, and finishing noodles. No plant-only preparation area or vegan accommodation is referenced in any source.

One non-Japanese reviewer noted staff attempted to assist with translation and communication at the table, suggesting some goodwill toward guests with special needs. However, no formal allergen protocol or allergy-handling procedure is documented in any public source.
